notes: Sixth sweep (2026-10-23, run head d04061d, uncommitted false): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript reads SKILL.md, the input and references/ex_unit.md with Read (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read SKILL.md and the input twice), matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md) is met in 5 of 5. Graded against the previous sweep's grades (sweeps/2026-10-22-d/grades/log-tests-*.json, at ba24972). git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ shows two changes: SKILL.md gains paragraphs under "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys" and a rewrite of "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" (neither in this case's list), and ex_unit.md's "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" gains one closing sentence.

"Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" changed; graded against the current text. The only new sentence is "A crash report's content depends on the primary level alone: `Logger.Translator` prints the `State:` line and the client's stacktrace only when `Logger.level/0` is `:debug`, and a module level does not change that, so a test of what a crash report carries also needs `Logger.configure/1` and `async: false`." No run tests a crash report, so that sentence decides no verdict here (0 of 5 runs violating; not exercised in 5 of 5). Per sentence of the rule, the count of runs violating: capture with capture_log/2 or with_log/2 rather than a handler, StringIO or backend, 0 of 5; pass the formatter's options for format and metadata, 0 of 5 (every run passes :metadata; opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 also pass :format, sonnet-1 keeps the default format); run under async: true, 0 of 5; wrap every call that logs, return-value tests included, 0 of 5 (sonnet-1 lines 61 and 92 and sonnet-2 lines 38, 57 and 79 wrap return-value tests in an option-less capture_log only to silence them, which the sentence asks for); primary-level and Logger.put_module_level sentence, not exercised in 5 of 5; crash-report sentence, not exercised in 5 of 5. The caller's per-bullet instruction names webhook-parser.md and library-client.md; log-tests.md has no per-sentence bullets, so the counts above follow the rule's own sentences.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state", "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", "Assert with patterns" and "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" are unchanged since ba24972 and graded to the 2026-10-22-d standard; all four are clean in 5 of 5. All five use async: true with no Logger.configure, Process.register or application env. opus-1 uses a single describe "charge/3"; the other four use describe "charge/3" plus a condition. opus-1's names "returns :declined and logs ..." and "returns :unavailable and logs ..." name the returned error and what was logged, so they are not the "returns :ok" shape. Assert with patterns: opus-1, sonnet-2 and sonnet-1 (lines 48-49) put the call itself on the left of ==; sonnet-1 lines 37-39, 62-64 and 93-95 bind result = Charger.charge(...) and then assert result == {...}, the "result bound a line earlier" case the rule's == sentence names, so not counted as "a match that binds the value and an == on it afterwards", as in 2026-10-22-d; haiku-1 matches the result bound by an exempt with_log destructure with assert {...} = result. The only bare matches are with_log destructures (haiku-1 lines 42, 54, 68) or destructures of a helper returning with_log's tuple (haiku-2 lines 42, 58, 74), which the rule exempts. Every run uses one Payments.Gateway module per outcome (opus-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2 nested in the test module; haiku-1 and haiku-2 as top-level Payments.ChargerTest.* modules).

Success-case absence: sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 assert an empty level: :warning capture; opus-1 captures at level: :warning and refutes its own request id (lines 47, 51), with a comment that under async: true a capture can hold other modules' lines; haiku-1 and haiku-2 refute ~r/\[(warning|error)\]/, which leaves out critical, alert and emergency, as haiku-1 did in 2026-10-22-d. All met the check.

Outside the case's list, no violation counted in any run. One borderline shape not counted: haiku-2 lines 83-88 pass a three-option keyword literal inline to with_log/2 inside a helper whose result is returned, not bound; the transcript shows the run wrote with_log([format: @log_format, metadata: [...], colors: [enabled: false]], fn -> on one line and mix format spread the call over six lines. "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" defines the case as "a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines", and this literal stays on one line (line 84), so I did not count it; if the rule means any literal long enough to force the call to wrap, the sentence should say so. Wraps after == (haiku-1 lines 61-62, sonnet-1 lines 48-49, sonnet-2 lines 39-40, 47-48, 58-59, 66-67, 80-81, 88-89) are the formatter's own wrap after an operator and not counted. The new SKILL.md head-binding and required-keys text is not exercised: no multi-clause function and no body pattern pulling one field. Not reported, as before: gateway modules without @moduledoc false (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1) in an .exs script that builds no docs. All five ran mix format --check-formatted on the file during the session.

Tests were run from copies in the grader scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each with ExUnit's random seed: every file passed every time (opus-1 and haiku-1 3 tests each, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 6, sonnet-1 7) with no compiler warning and no log line printed. All five pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json. As in 2026-10-22-d, each file was run against five mutants of the input (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error): every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so no log assertion is vacuous.
